verdicts.line: You can roar — and everyone who witnesses it will fear you, whatever you intend.
verdicts.quoted_chunk: the roar frightens all who witness it, whatever you intend
verdicts.reason: Direct instrumentation that names the verb, states the unconditional Fear consequence, and preserves the 'whatever you intend' paradox central to uhta's design.

verdicts.line: Roar. The earth shatters ahead of you, and everyone who sees it is frightened — even if your flame burns hope.
verdicts.quoted_chunk: the roar frightens all who witness it, whatever you intend
verdicts.reason: Names the verb imperatively, states terrain effect and witness consequence, and preserves the hope-flame exception paradox with 'even if your flame burns hope'.

verdicts.line: This is the roar. It frightens all who witness it, no matter what your flame carries.
verdicts.quoted_chunk: the roar frightens all who witness it, whatever you intend
verdicts.reason: Loses the terrain-shattering effect entirely and 'what your flame carries' is vague where the chunk specifies 'whatever you intend' as the paradox.
verdicts.correction: This is the roar. It shatters the ground ahead, and frightens all who witness it — whatever you intend.

verdicts.line: You roar to shatter the ground — but know this: everyone within sight will fear you, regardless of your light.
verdicts.quoted_chunk: Shatters a line of tiles — fast traversal / path creation
verdicts.reason: 'Clears distance fast' is missing from the chunk vocabulary; 'within sight' dilutes the witness-radius mechanic to generic visibility.
verdicts.correction: You roar to shatter a line through the ground — but everyone who witnesses it will fear you, whatever you intend.

verdicts.line: The roar clears distance fast, but whoever witnesses the line takes fear — your flame's color cannot protect them.
verdicts.quoted_chunk: Shatters a line of tiles — fast traversal / path creation. NPCs within witness radius R (~6 tiles) of the line take an unconditional Fear push
verdicts.reason: Names fast traversal, states the unconditional Fear mechanic, and preserves the flame-color-cannot-override paradox with instrumentation register.

verdicts.line: Roar, and the stone breaks open — yet every soul who sees you do it learns fear, whether you mean them to or not.
verdicts.quoted_chunk: the roar frightens all who witness it, whatever you intend
verdicts.reason: 'Every soul who sees you do it learns fear' mythologizes where the tutorial demands instrumentation; 'learns fear' is pedagogical metaphor, not mechanical consequence.
verdicts.correction: Roar, and the stone breaks open — but everyone who witnesses it takes fear, whatever you intend.

verdicts.line: You can roar a path through the earth. Everyone who watches will be pushed toward fear. Your intention does not matter.
verdicts.quoted_chunk: the roar frightens all who witness it, whatever you intend
verdicts.reason: Names the verb, states terrain effect and witness consequence as push toward Fear, and closes with the intention-paradox in plain instrumentation.

verdicts.line: This is roar: it splits the ground and makes witnesses afraid, even when your flame is green.
verdicts.quoted_chunk: the roar frightens all who witness it, whatever you intend
verdicts.reason: Tutorial naming ('This is roar'), states both terrain and Fear effects, and preserves the flame-color exception with concrete 'even when your flame is green'.
